title: Residency enforcement: testing corpus and runbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working corpus + runbook for validating region pinning and residency enforcement behavior end-to-end. Focus is on observable, repeatable tests that exercise policy evaluation, routing, fallback, and audit logging for Hosted/Dedicated/Private modes. This doc is intentionally implementation-focused: small test payloads, exact header examples, acceptance criteria, and telemetry assertions.

Goals:
- Provide a compact set of test vectors that cover common and edge pinning scenarios (customer-specified pin, geo-IP, org policy, export exception).
- Define automated and manual checks for enforcement correctness and minimal disruption (latency, error behavior).
- Surface required telemetry and retention needs for compliance audits.
- Offer a staging rollout plan with rollback gates and clear owners.

Assumptions:
- Runtime exposes X-Region-Pin and X-Fallback-Reason in request/response headers for test builds.
- Audit logs are persisted to the customer tenant storage and to central S3 bucket for 90 days in staging.
- Test cluster can simulate region outages and introduce routing latency.

Non-functional acceptance criteria (must meet during tests):
- Enforcement accuracy: 99.95% of requests with explicit pin header are served from pinned region or rejected with documented error.
- Fallback transparency: When fallback occurs, response includes X-Fallback-Reason and audit entry within 30s.
- Latency SLO regression: 95th percentile latency for pinned requests not > 1.5x unpinned baseline in staging.
- No silent cross-border leakage: all request and response bodies containing PII must remain within pinned region or be redacted per policy.

Quick reference headers (test harness will use these):
- X-Region-Pin: eu-west-1  (explicit customer pin)
- X-Region-Policy: residency:eu
- X-User-IP: 203.0.113.45  (simulated client IP — used for geo-IP mapping tests)
- Authorization: Bearer <test-token>  (tokens that map to orgs in different jurisdictions)

Test vectors (minimal set) — each vector includes: intent, request headers, payload note, expected outcome, telemetry to assert.

1) Explicit pin, compliant region
- Intent: Customer requests eu residency explicitly.
- Headers: X-Region-Pin: eu-west-1, X-User-IP: 203.0.113.45
- Payload: simple chat prompt with PII (name + email)
- Expected: Served from eu-west-1, response success 200, response contains X-Region-Pin: eu-west-1, audit log entry with field residency=pinned_eu
- Telemetry: pinned_count +1, routing_latency < baseline*1.2, audit_log_written=true

2) Explicit pin, pinned region unavailable -> fallback allowed by policy
- Intent: Test graceful fallback path when pinned region out of capacity but policy allows fallthrough.
- Headers: X-Region-Pin: us-east-1 (simulate outage in us-east-1), X-Region-Policy: allow-fallback:region-equivalent
- Expected: Return 200 served from fallback region (us-west-2), response includes X-Fallback-Reason: capacity_unavailable, audit contains fallback_to=us-west-2, fallback_count increments
- Telemetry: fallback_rate <= 5% for simulated outage, fallback_latency measured, alert if fallback_rate > threshold

3) Explicit pin, strict residency (no fallback) -> should reject
- Intent: Org-level strict residency (regulatory).
- Headers: X-Region-Pin: ap-southeast-1, X-Region-Policy: residency:strict
- Setup: Simulate ap-southeast-1 maintenance (unavailable)
- Expected: API returns 409 or 451 (configurable) with body explaining "pinned region unavailable, strict residency prevents fallback"; audit log entry records rejection and request id
- Telemetry: rejection_count++, error_rate_by_org alerts if > 0.1% over baseline during test window

4) Geo-IP indicates local residency but organization-level pin conflicts (pin wins)
- Intent: Ensure explicit pin takes precedence over geo-IP mapping.
- Headers: X-User-IP: 198.51.100.22 (maps to eu), X-Region-Pin: us-east-1
- Expected: Serve from us-east-1, telemetry indicates override_reason=explicit_pin

5) Data export exception route (legal order)
- Intent: Exercise path that allows cross-border export for named exception with audit markers.
- Headers: X-Region-Pin: eu-west-1, X-Region-Policy: allow-export:case-42, X-Export-Token: <signed-token>
- Expected: Service allows cross-region processing but response includes X-Export-Audit: case-42, audit payload signed, retention flag set

Edge cases and fuzzing set:
- Missing tenant mapping: request should be rejected with 401 and audit entry
- Malformed pin header: ignore header and fallback to org policy, log parse_error
- High token-length prompts that change kernel selection; validate that KV cache stays colocated with pinned region

Operator runbook (manual steps for critical tests)
- Pre-test: ensure staging audit-bucket has fresh credentials and retention policy set to 90d; run infra sanity: ./scripts/check-pinning-config.sh
- Start scenario 2 (fallback allowed): enable region outage simulation toggle in chaos-grid for target region; run 1000 synthetic requests with explicit pin; monitor fallback_count and X-Fallback-Reason in responses
- On unexpected behavior: capture request_id, route path, kernel trace (if available), and escalate to oncall with tag residency-critical
- Post-test: run audit verification script to reconcile audit logs vs. central telemetry: ./tools/reconcile-audits --since 2025-01-12T00:00Z --tenant test-tenant-42

Telemetry and log expectations (staging)
- Minimum telemetry fields per request: request_id, tenant_id, org_residency_policy, effective_region, pin_header, routing_path, fallback_reason (nullable), audit_log_pointer
- Acceptable delays: audit entry available in central index within 30s for 95% of events
- Dashboards to validate: Residency enforcement (pinned vs unpinned), Fallbacks by region and tenant, Rejections (strict policy) over time, Cross-border audit trail

Postmortem and audit checklist (for compliance review)
- For each test run capture: list of request ids, raw audit artifacts (signed), operators who triggered tests, exact infra toggles used, and sha of runtime deployed
- Export bundle format: zip containing run_manifest.json (plain text table), audit_records.ndjson, test_outputs.tgz, and run_notes.md

Open questions / decisions to make (requires legal/product):
- Minimum audit retention for customer-facing proofs: 90d vs 365d? (legal leaning toward 365d for EU enterprise deals)
- Standard error code for strict residency rejection: 451 vs 409? (451 signals legal/unavailable for legal reasons)
- Should fallback be rate-limited per-tenant automatically or only under incident?

Staging rollout plan (gated):
- Phase 0: Unit-level policy tests on dev nodes (owner: Priya)
- Phase 1: Integration tests in staging with synthetic corpus (owner: Avery)
- Gate A: All audit logs reconcile, fallback_rate <= 1% in synthetic outage sim
- Phase 2: Canary in dedicated cluster with 1% real traffic (customer opt-in) — monitor for 24h (owner: Diego)
- Gate B: No unexplained rejections, 95th percentile latency within threshold, legal sign-off on audit retention
- Phase 3: Full rollout with migrated telemetry dashboards and runbook published

Next steps (owner: Avery):
1) Convert these vectors into automated tests in residency-test-harness repo (ticket JIRA-RES-4123)
2) Add X-Fallback-Reason to public SDK stub for easier debugging (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/PR-789)
3) Sync with Legal on retention minimum; schedule 30-min sync (Maya to lead)
4) Bake audit-reconcile job into CI nightly pipeline for staging

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: the goal is run/observe/fix quickly rather than a perfect spec. Add missing edge cases you hit; annotate tests with actual telemetry keys you used.

-- end of doc --
